about: Minimized regression vectors of the issue #196 differential fuzz: one or more per divergence category the campaign found, and agreement vectors at boundaries the generated corpus reaches rarely (`agrees`: why both sides answer alike). `origin` says where a vector came from: the campaign case it was minimized from, or that it was written by hand (for a category, naming the category's first run-3 case). Each runs in its own environment (its `did`); the Rust driver records the reference verdict into tests/goldens/differential/corpus.jsonl, and the TypeScript replay holds each to the category listed for it in tests/goldens/differential/divergences.json, or to agreement.

vectors.name: leb128_overlong_nat_value
vectors.note: nat 5 as the two-byte group 85 00. Reference accepts 5; the runtime refuses overlong_leb128 (intended, #103 decision 4).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is d/1000000/7

vectors.name: leb128_overlong_type_count
vectors.note: An empty type table whose count is the two-byte group 80 00. Reference accepts; the runtime refuses in the header (intended, #103 decision 4).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is d/1000000/7

vectors.name: leb128_wide_field_id
vectors.note: Field id 97 ("a") as a six-byte group e1 80 80 80 80 00: longer than a u32 field's five bytes, so the runtime reports invalid_length; the reference accepts. Same rule, non-minimal LEB128 (intended).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is d/1000000/7

vectors.name: empty_method_name
vectors.note: A func reference to aaaaa-aa with an empty method name. Reference accepts; the runtime refuses invalid_length by decision (round-trip symmetry with validate and encode; candid-core's HostValue validator refuses it too).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is d/1000005/5

vectors.name: empty_method_under_absorbed_opt
vectors.note: A func reference with an empty method name inside an opt record whose other field (text) the expected type (nat) refuses. The reference absorbs the opt to null and never decodes the func; the runtime refuses the empty method name first (invalid_length, a hard error). The empty-method decision, flagged from the bytes (empty_method).
vectors.origin: minimized from d/1026525/78 (the fix-round re-classification of run 3)
vectors.did:
type W = opt record { func () -> (); text };
type E = opt record { func () -> (); nat };

vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is c/1000002/11

vectors.name: contract_orphan_type_node

vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is c/1000000/8

vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is c/1001109/14

vectors.name: contract_identities_edit
vectors.note: A contract id that is not a contract id. Contract::from_json refuses it; schemaFromContract does not read identities, by design (contract.ts).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is c/1000014/5

vectors.name: contract_producer_edit

vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is c/1000120/12

vectors.name: reference_refuses_identical_func
vectors.note: A func reference written and read at the same type func (L) -> () with L = record { a : L }. The candid crate rewrites the uninhabited record L in the wire table to empty (TypeEnv::replace_empty) but not in the expected type, so its subtype check becomes L <: empty and fails: it refuses identical types. The runtime accepts. Reference bug.
vectors.did:
type L = record { a : L };
type F = func (L) -> ();

vectors.name: reference_absorbs_identical_func_in_opt
vectors.note: The same func reference under opt, read at its own type: the reference's failed subtype check is absorbed by the opt, so it decodes null; the runtime decodes the reference. Reference bug (same cause).

vectors.name: reference_accepts_non_subtype_func
vectors.note: A func () -> (W) read at func () -> (E) with W = record { x : W } and E = record { y : E }: W lacks E's required field y, so the wire type is not a subtype. The reference rewrites W to empty and accepts (empty <: E); the runtime refuses type_mismatch. Reference bug (same cause, the other direction).

vectors.name: reference_skips_invalid_utf8_method
vectors.note: An extra func argument whose method name is the single byte ff (not UTF-8), skipped because no argument is expected. The reference skips it without checking (it does check a skipped text, and refuses this name when it decodes the func); the runtime refuses invalid_utf8. Reference bug.

vectors.name: future_type_reference_count
vectors.note: A value of a future type (opcode -2462, no data bytes) that declares one reference, read at reserved. The reference skips it; the runtime refuses invalid_principal: reference sequences are unsupported by this codec, as documented (intended).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is d/1003813/35

vectors.name: reference_quota_skipped_vec
vectors.note: An extra argument of type vec null with 10,114 elements, skipped. Skipping charges the reference's decoding quota 50x, which exhausts the harness's first quota (2,000,000); the scan counts 10,115 values, within wire::RETRY_VALUES, so the reference is decoded again under a quota sized to the message and accepts. Until the retry (issue #196 review), this was decode:intended:reference-quota.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: the quota retry lets the reference finish a message within the runtime's element budget.

vectors.name: contract_declarations_absent
vectors.note: A Contract document with its empty declarations key removed. Contract::from_json accepts it (the key defaults to empty); schemaFromContract refuses invalid_contract_document (declarations must be an array).
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is c/1006849/5

vectors.name: reference_reads_func_from_empty_wire
vectors.note: One argument whose wire type is empty, followed by the bytes of a func reference, read at a func type. No value has type empty, yet the reference decodes aaaaa-aa.f: it reads a reference value through its subtype relation alone, where empty <: t holds. The runtime refuses type_mismatch. Reference bug.
vectors.origin: written by hand for its category, whose first run-3 case is d/1012392/198

vectors.name: reference_unsound_subtype_memo
vectors.note: func () -> (W3) read at func () -> (E3). W7 <: E7 is false (W5 has an arm x that V lacks), and the reference refuses W7 at E7 on its own; but checking W3 <: E3 visits c : opt W5 first, assumes (W5, V), proves (W7, E7) under that assumption, retracts (W5, V) when x fails (the opt rule then accepts c), and keeps (W7, E7) in its memo, so v : W7 <: E7 is answered true. The runtime refuses type_mismatch. Reference bug (unsound coinductive memo).

vectors.name: label_collision_numbered_field
vectors.note: record { x : record { 100 : text } } where another declaration writes the same canonical record as record { d : text } (the label hash of d is 100). The field-name table attaches names to canonical nodes, so the runtime keys B's field as d; the reference (and the source) say 100. Same bytes, same id, different domain key.
vectors.did:
type A = record { c : record { d : text } };
type B = record { x : record { 100 : text } };

vectors.name: validate_hostvalue_nesting_limit
vectors.note: A vec nested 40 levels deep at type T = vec T. Its HostValue JSON nests 80 containers, past the HostValue JSON decoder's max_value_nesting (64); the driver rebuilds the value through the HostValue constructors (max_value_depth 256, validate's maxDepth) and validate_host_value accepts it, as validate does. Until the rebuild (issue #196 review), the JSON cap stood in for the reference's verdict (validate:intended:limit-policy).
vectors.agrees: Both accept: the reference judges the value rebuilt through the HostValue constructors.

vectors.name: depth_opt_127_levels
vectors.note: opt T0 nested 127 levels (126 present, the innermost absent): 254 depth steps, within the runtime's maxDepth of 256.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: inside the runtime's maxDepth.

vectors.name: depth_opt_128_levels
vectors.note: opt T0 nested 128 levels: 256 depth steps, exactly the runtime's maxDepth.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: exactly at the runtime's maxDepth.

vectors.name: depth_opt_129_levels
vectors.note: opt T0 nested 129 levels: 258 depth steps, past the runtime's maxDepth; the reference (bounded only by its stack) accepts. Intended (decode:intended:ts-limit), flagged deep_nesting.

vectors.name: depth_variant_127_levels
vectors.note: variant { a : T0; b } nested 127 levels, the innermost arm b: 2 x 127 + 1 = 255 depth steps, within maxDepth.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: inside the runtime's maxDepth.
vectors.did: type T0 = variant { a : T0; b };

vectors.name: depth_variant_128_levels
vectors.note: variant { a : T0; b } nested 128 levels: 257 depth steps, one past maxDepth. Intended (decode:intended:ts-limit), flagged deep_nesting.
vectors.did: type T0 = variant { a : T0; b };

vectors.name: depth_coercion_inserted_opts
vectors.note: vec T0 nested 90 levels, read at T2 = vec opt T2: the coercion inserts an opt at every level, so the expected-side value nests about 180 levels although the wire nests 90. The runtime refuses past its maxDepth; the reference accepts. Intended (decode:intended:ts-limit), flagged deep_nesting from the decoded value, not the wire.
vectors.origin: minimized from xd/5000009/2 (fix-round campaign, new generator)
vectors.did:
type T0 = vec T0;
type T2 = vec opt T2;

vectors.name: nat_minimal_two_bytes
vectors.note: nat 128 as its minimal two-byte group 80 01: a minimality check that also refused a minimal group would turn this into a divergence.

vectors.name: principal_29_bytes
vectors.note: A principal of 29 bytes, the longest id: a length cap below 29 would turn this into a divergence.

vectors.name: bool_byte_two
vectors.note: A bool encoded as 02. Both refuse: a bool is 00 or 01.

vectors.name: text_invalid_utf8
vectors.note: A text of the single byte ff (not UTF-8). Both refuse.

vectors.name: validate_missing_required_field
vectors.note: A record value without its required field b. Both refuse.
vectors.did: type T0 = record { a : nat; b : text };

vectors.name: elements_skipped_vec_499999
vectors.note: An extra argument of type vec null with 499,999 elements, skipped. The scan counts 500,000 values, not more than half maxElements, so the message is not flagged many_values: an element-budget refusal here is a plain symptom (decode:ts-rejects:resource_limit_exceeded), never ts-limit.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: within half the runtime's maxElements.

vectors.name: elements_skipped_vec_999999
vectors.note: An extra argument of type vec null with 999,999 elements, skipped: the runtime charges the vec and each element, 1,000,000, exactly its maxElements.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: exactly at the runtime's maxElements.

vectors.name: elements_skipped_vec_1000000
vectors.note: An extra argument of type vec null with 1,000,000 elements, skipped: 1,000,001 charges, one past maxElements; the runtime refuses (resource value_elements), the reference (retried under a quota sized to the message) accepts. Intended (decode:intended:ts-limit), flagged many_values.

vectors.name: reference_quota_forged_length
vectors.note: An extra argument of type vec null with a forged length of 2^40, skipped. The scan stops counting at 4,000,000 values, past wire::RETRY_VALUES, so the reference is not retried and its first quota runs out (class limit); the runtime refuses at its element budget.
vectors.agrees: Both refuse: a limit on each side, which agree with any rejection.

vectors.name: chain_opt_127_levels
vectors.note: A chain of 127 declarations T0 = opt T1, …, T126 = opt T127, T127 = nat, and a value present at every level: 2 x 127 + 1 = 255 depth steps (the runtime charges a declaration reference like a rec hop), within maxDepth.
vectors.agrees: Both accept: inside the runtime's maxDepth.

vectors.name: chain_opt_128_levels
vectors.note: A chain of 128 declarations T0 = opt T1, …, T127 = opt T128, T128 = nat, and a value present at every level: 2 x 128 + 1 = 257 depth steps, one past maxDepth; the reference accepts. Intended (decode:intended:ts-limit), flagged deep_nesting.

vectors.note: vec T nested 128 levels at type T = vec T: validate charges each level a constructor step and a rec hop, 256 depth steps, exactly its maxDepth; the HostValue JSON nests past the decoder's 64-container cap, so the reference judges the value rebuilt through the HostValue constructors.

vectors.name: validate_depth_vec_129_levels

vectors.name: validate_depth_vec_257_levels

vectors.name: validate_depth_vec_258_levels
